Sample Sizes for a Cluster Randomized Design: Accuracy in Parameter Estimation for the Difference Between Condition Means

Source: R/ss_aipe_crd.R
ss_aipe_crd.Rd

Finds the number of clusters, the number of individuals per cluster, or both, for a two-condition cluster randomized design (CRD), so that the confidence interval for the difference between the condition means has a desired width or is as narrow as a budget allows. Four of the functions fix one of the two sizes and take a desired width or a budget; the two both functions take a budget and return the sizes that give the narrowest interval, or take a desired width and return the least costly sizes.

ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_width(
  width,
  cluster_size,
  pr_treat,
  true_var_between = NULL,
  true_var_within = NULL,
  true_total_var = NULL,
  true_icc = NULL,
  true_R2_between = 0,
  true_R2_within = 0,
  n_covariates = 0,
  assurance = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  cluster_cost = NULL,
  individual_cost = NULL,
  diff_size = NULL
)

ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_width(

  n_clusters,
  pr_treat,

Arguments

width

The desired width of the confidence interval of the unstandardized means difference

cluster_size

The number of individuals in each cluster: a single whole number of at least 2. The searches over the cluster size start at 2, and with one individual in a cluster the variance between clusters cannot be told from the variance within them

pr_treat

The proportion of treatment clusters: a single number strictly between 0 and 1

true_var_between

The population residual variance in the between level before accounting for the covariate (a planning value), 0 or more

true_var_within

The population residual variance in the within level before accounting for the covariate (a planning value), 0 or more

true_total_var

The population total residual variance before accounting for the covariate (a planning value), positive. Any two of true_var_between, true_var_within, true_total_var, and true_icc determine the other two; a third or fourth must agree with them (see the section on refused calls)

true_icc

The population intraclass correlation of the dependent variable (a planning value), the share of true_total_var that lies between clusters, in [0, 1]

true_R2_between

The population proportion of the between-level variance that the cluster-level covariates explain (a planning value in [0, 1); default 0). It must be 0 when n_covariates = 0, since there is then no covariate at the cluster level to explain it

true_R2_within

The population proportion of the within-level variance that the covariates explain (a planning value in [0, 1); default 0, no covariate)

n_covariates

The number of covariates at the cluster (between) level, not counting the treatment indicator: a single whole number of 0 or more. The degrees of freedom of the interval are n_clusters - 2 - n_covariates. The default, 0, is a model with the treatment indicator alone. It is not p, the total number of predictors, which here is p = n_covariates + 1.

assurance

The degree of assurance, which is the value with which confidence can be placed that describes the likelihood of obtaining a confidence interval less than the value specified (e.g., .80, .90, .95)

conf_level

The desired level of confidence for the confidence interval

cluster_cost

The cost of adding one cluster, whatever the number of individuals in it: a single finite number of 0 or more. Where the costs choose the design (the two budget functions that fix a size and the two both functions), cluster_cost and individual_cost cannot both be 0

individual_cost

The cost of adding one individual to a cluster: a single finite number of 0 or more, and positive where the costs choose the cluster size (ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_budget and the two both functions), since otherwise clusters of every size cost the same

diff_size

Difference cluster size specification. The differences in cluster sizes can be specified in two ways, and the specified vector is recycled across the clusters. First, users may specify differences as integers, which can be negative or positive; the resulting cluster sizes add the specified values to the estimated cluster size. For example, if the cluster size is 25, the number of clusters is 10, and diff_size = c(-1, 0, 1), the cluster sizes will be 24, 25, 26, 24, 25, 26, 24, 25, 26, and 24. Second, users may specify multipliers of the cluster size as positive decimals; at least one value must be non-integer, which is what selects the multiplicative form. The resulting cluster sizes multiply the estimated cluster size by the specified values and round to the nearest integer. For example, if the cluster size is 25, the number of clusters is 10, and diff_size = c(0.8, 1, 1.2), the cluster sizes will be 20, 25, 30, 20, 25, 30, 20, 25, 30, and 20. In either form a resulting cluster size below 1 is set to 1. If NULL, the cluster size is equal across clusters. Anything other than NULL or a vector of one or more finite numbers is refused

n_clusters

The number of clusters: a single whole number of at least 3 + n_covariates, since the interval has n_clusters - 2 - n_covariates degrees of freedom. With pr_treat it must put a cluster in each condition (round(n_clusters * pr_treat) of them are treated)

budget

The amount available for the study, in the units of cluster_cost and individual_cost: a single finite number of 0 or more. A budget that does not buy the smallest design the function considers is refused (see the section on refused calls)

Value

The ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_width and ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget functions provide the number of clusters. The ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_width and ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_budget functions provide the cluster size. The ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_budget and ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_width provide the number of clusters and the cluster size, respectively.

Each returns a table with the columns term and value. The rows, where they apply, are necessary_n_clusters (the number of clusters, where it is solved for), necessary_cluster_size (the number of individuals in each cluster, where it is solved for; with diff_size the cluster sizes and their frequencies are printed ahead of the table instead), width (the desired width, in the functions that plan from one), the width of the interval the design gives, and budget (the cost of the design, when the two costs are supplied). Without assurance the width row is expected_width, the expected width of the interval. With assurance it is assured_width, the width that the interval does not exceed with the requested probability, followed by the row assurance that echoes that probability.

A size that was given is an argument of the call and is not repeated in the table: only a size the function solved for has a row, and its name begins with necessary_. tidy and glance report the planned size as estimate (the number of clusters where it was solved for, otherwise the cluster size) and the desired width as width, which is NA for a plan made from a budget; glance() carries expected_width or assured_width as a column of that name.

Details

Here are the functions' descriptions:

ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_width

Find the number of clusters given a specified width of the confidence interval and the cluster size

ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_width

Find the cluster size given a specified width of the confidence interval and the number of clusters

ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget

Find the number of clusters given a budget and the cluster size

ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_budget

Find the cluster size given a budget and the number of clusters

ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_budget

Find the sample size combinations (the number of clusters and that cluster size) providing the narrowest confidence interval given the fixed budget

ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_width

Find the sample size combinations (the number of clusters and that cluster size) providing the lowest cost given the specified width of the confidence interval

The searches over the number of clusters consider at least ceiling(2 / min(pr_treat, 1 - pr_treat)) + n_covariates clusters, which puts at least two clusters in each condition after rounding (the rule of MBESS; Kelley, 2007a, 2007b) and gives the interval at least two degrees of freedom: 4 clusters at pr_treat = 0.5, 20 at 0.1, and 200 at 0.01. From there ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_width returns the smallest number of clusters whose width is no larger than width (a width equal to the target meets it, so asking for the width a plan reports returns that plan), and the two both functions compare numbers of clusters from there with cluster sizes of 2 or more. The searches consider at most 1,000,000 clusters, the bound the power planners use for a sample size: the width falls toward 0 as clusters are added, so every positive target is met by some number, but a target too narrow for any study would otherwise be searched for without end. The widths at 100, 200, ..., 1000 clusters bracket the target, and the bracket is searched one cluster at a time, which gives the smallest number when the width falls as clusters are added, as it does with equal cluster sizes and no assurance. At an assurance below .5 the width need not fall as the number of clusters grows, so the search may return more than the smallest number that meets the target; the same can happen with unequal cluster sizes (diff_size), whose width depends on how the sizes fall between the conditions. The cluster size searches consider 2 to 100,000 individuals per cluster.

Refused calls

Each refusal below is an error of class dmar_argument_invalid that names the argument or arguments as arg and, where the cause needs a name, gives it as reason.

  • n_covariates must be a whole number of 0 or more, cluster_size a whole number of at least 2, and n_clusters a whole number of at least 3 + n_covariates; pr_treat must be strictly between 0 and 1, and true_R2_between and true_R2_within in [0, 1). A nonzero true_R2_between with n_covariates = 0 is refused with reason "R2_between_without_covariates"; true_R2_within may be nonzero without them. A number of clusters that, at pr_treat, leaves a condition without a cluster is refused with reason "arm_without_clusters". diff_size must be NULL or a vector of one or more finite numbers.

  • Each cost, and the budget, must be a single finite number of 0 or more. Costs that are both 0 are refused where the costs choose the design (reason "costs_all_zero"), and individual_cost = 0 where they choose the cluster size (reason "individual_cost_zero"): a search over designs that all cost the same has no end. In the two functions that plan from a width and a fixed size the costs only price the design, and costs of 0 give a budget of 0.

  • A budget that does not buy the smallest design the function can return is refused with reason "budget_infeasible" and the cost of that design as min_cost: in ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget 4 clusters of cluster_size, or, with pr_treat, the fewest clusters that put a cluster in each condition and leave a degree of freedom (6 at pr_treat = 0.1); in ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_budget n_clusters clusters of 2; and in ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_budget the fewest clusters its search considers, given above, each of 2. When ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget is given pr_treat and the budget buys 4 clusters or more but a design with no finite width, it is refused with reason "arm_without_clusters" (a condition without a cluster) or "too_few_clusters" (no degrees of freedom), with the budget that buys the fewest clusters that would do.

  • ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_width refuses a width that no cluster size up to 100,000 reaches with n_clusters clusters, with reason "width_not_reachable"; it gives as width_limit the width the interval falls toward as the clusters grow, which the variance between clusters sets, and says whether a larger cluster size would reach the target. ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_width and ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_width refuse a width that no design of up to 1,000,000 clusters meets (with clusters of up to 100,000 individuals in the latter), with reason "n_clusters_beyond_reach" and the width there as width_at_max.

  • The variances are needed where a width is computed: two of true_var_between, true_var_within, true_total_var, and true_icc, any two (reason "underidentified_variances" otherwise, as for a between-cluster variance of 0 with an intraclass correlation of 0). Each must be NULL or a single finite number (reason "variance_input_invalid"). A variance must be 0 or more, the total variance positive (whether it is given or is the sum of the two variances, so two variances of 0 are refused), and the intraclass correlation in [0, 1] (reason "variance_out_of_range"). A third or fourth value must agree with the two that determine the model to within about 1e-14 of its scale (reason "inconsistent_variances", with the value they imply in the message), so a rounded value is refused; give two and leave the others NULL. With diff_size the variance within clusters must be positive (reason "within_variance_zero"). These refusals carry the four values as given in supplied.

References

Kelley, K. (2007a). Confidence intervals for standardized effect sizes: Theory, application, and implementation. Journal of Statistical Software, 20(8), 1–24. doi:10.18637/jss.v020.i08

Kelley, K. (2007b). Methods for the behavioral, educational, and social sciences: An R package. Behavior Research Methods, 39(4), 979–984. doi:10.3758/BF03192993

Pornprasertmanit, S., & Schneider, W. J. (2014). Accuracy in parameter estimation in cluster randomized designs. Psychological Methods, 19(3), 356–379. doi:10.1037/a0037036

See also

design_consequences for what a chosen design delivers: power, the Type S (sign) and Type M (exaggeration) errors of the significance filter, and the expected confidence interval width.

Examples

# Examples for each function
ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_width(width = 0.3, cluster_size = 30,
  pr_treat = 0.5, true_var_between = 0.25, true_var_within = 0.75)
#>  term                 value
#>  necessary_n_clusters 191  
#>  width                0.300
#>  expected_width       0.299
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_width(width = 0.3, n_clusters = 250,
  pr_treat = 0.5, true_var_between = 0.25, true_var_within = 0.75)
#>  term                   value
#>  necessary_cluster_size 7    
#>  width                  0.300
#>  expected_width         0.298
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget(budget = 10000, cluster_size = 20,
  cluster_cost = 20, individual_cost = 1)
#>  term                 value
#>  necessary_n_clusters 250  
#>  budget               10000
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_budget(budget = 10000, n_clusters = 30,
  cluster_cost = 20, individual_cost = 1,
  pr_treat = 0.5, true_var_between = 0.05, true_var_within = 0.95, assurance = 0.8)
#>  term                   value
#>  necessary_cluster_size 313  
#>  assured_width          0.380
#>  assurance              0.800
#>  budget                 9990 
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_budget(budget = 10000, cluster_cost = 30, individual_cost = 1,
  pr_treat = 0.5, true_var_between = 0.25, true_var_within = 0.75)
#>  term                   value
#>  necessary_n_clusters   250  
#>  necessary_cluster_size 10   
#>  expected_width         0.284
#>  budget                 10000
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_width(width = 0.3, cluster_cost = 0, individual_cost = 1,
  pr_treat = 0.5, true_var_between = 0.25, true_var_within = 0.75)
#>  term                   value
#>  necessary_n_clusters   430  
#>  necessary_cluster_size 2    
#>  width                  0.300
#>  expected_width         0.300
#>  budget                 860  
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

# Examples for different cluster size
set.seed(113)
ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_width(width = 0.3, cluster_size = 30,
